subject: Limitation of liability thresholds for ClearWave — proposed options
messages:
From: Michael Hart <michael.hart@bryantslaw.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@clearwavehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClearWave — proposed redlines to Order Form (liability cap)

Karthik / Laura,

Attached is ClearWave's counsel redline to the Order Form. Key commercial points:
- Liability cap: ClearWave proposes a cap equal to the greater of (a) total fees paid under the Order Form over the prior 12 months, or (b) USD 1,500,000.
- Exclusions: standard exclusions for fraud/willful misconduct to remain but they request a carve-out for data breach liabilities tied to consumer PII (they want an exception to the cap for that subset).
- Consequential damages: they seek to preserve consequential damages for losses arising from regulatory fines, breach notices, and customer claims directly tied to data exposures.

We redlined the Order Form with tracked changes and provided a short cover memo in the doc. Please confirm Redwood's position on annual vs total basis and whether you can accept the data-breach carve-out.

Attachments: OrderForm_Redline_CW_v1.docx (redline + counsel memo)

Regards,
Michael Hart
Bryants & Co. LLP

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearWave — proposed redlines to Order Form (liability cap)

Karthik — thanks for the ping. Summary of legal's posture after reviewing the redline and counselling with Ops: 

1) Cap basis: our preference is a cap tied to fees paid in the preceding 12 months (annualized) expressed as a multiple of annual fees rather than lifetime/total fees. That aligns limits with ongoing revenue and avoids open-ended lifetime exposure when engagements are multi-year.

2) Multiples: floor position is 1x annual fees for MSA-level liability (standard small-ticket deals); compromise range acceptable commercially: 2x–3x annual fees depending on term and customer tier. We should avoid a fixed large-dollar number unless Finance approves.

3) Data-breach carve-out: we should narrow any carve-out to liabilities arising from Redwood's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or failure to comply with our published security standards (SOC 2 controls). We should not accept a broad exception for all regulatory fines — that opens unlimited exposure.

4) Consequential damages: continue to exclude consequential damages except for payment obligations and direct regulatory fines that are demonstrably caused by Redwood's gross negligence. If they insist on preserving consequential damages generally, we should seek indemnity and caps tied to insurance limits.

Action items: 
- I'll prepare a redline to propose 2x annual fees as our starting compromise and explicitly carve the data-breach exception to gross negligence only.
- Rishi, can you confirm max tolerable exposure number (absolute dollar) so we can trade multiple vs cap floor.

Attachment: MSA_redline_LB_20260711.docx (tracked changes + rationale)

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearWave — proposed redlines to Order Form (liability cap)

Laura / Karthik — quick finance view: if we move to a 2x annual fees cap for this account (expected ARR year 1 ~ $700k), exposure is ~ $1.4M; at 3x it's $2.1M. Our loss modeling for worst-case security incident (not including cascading regulatory fines) suggests our retained risk (after insurance) should ideally stay below $2.5M per customer for this tier.

If legal wants 2x as the commercial compromise, finance is ok so long as we keep data-breach carve-outs tight and preserve deductibility from our cyber insurance. If we accept a higher uncapped exception for regulatory fines, that materially increases risk and requires senior approval.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@clearwavehealth.com>, Michael Hart <michael.hart@bryantslaw.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: liability cap options and recommended compromise

Sara / Michael — thanks again for the redline. After internal review we've outlined two practical paths to close quickly: 

Option A (preferred compromise):
- Liability cap: 2x of the annual fees invoiced in the 12 months preceding the claim (rolling 12-month).
- Data-breach carve-out: an exception only where Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct is established by clear evidence; regulatory fines remain subject to the cap unless tied to Redwood's gross negligence.
- Consequential damages: remain excluded except for payment obligations and direct regulatory fines tied to proven Redwood fault.

Option B (alternate):
- Liability cap: 3x annual fees OR USD 2,000,000 (whichever is lower).
- Data-breach carve-out: limited to consumer PII exposures and only where Redwood's obligations under the DPA are breached.

Rationale: Option A keeps the cap proportional to ongoing spend and simplifies long-term exposure modeling. Option B gives ClearWave a higher ceiling while protecting Redwood with a dollar cap. Finance/legal sign off on Option A or B with narrow carve-outs.

If you're comfortable, we can incorporate the agreed language into the Order Form and circulate for final sign-off and DocuSign. See attached proposed OrderForm_proposed_20260713.docx and a DocuSign stub below.

DocuSign link (preview): https://docusign.com/clearwave/orderform/abc123

Thanks — let me know which option you prefer and I'll have legal turn it into clean contract language.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: OrderForm_proposed_20260713.docx
From: Michael Hart <michael.hart@bryantslaw.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@clearwavehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: liability cap options and recommended compromise

Karthik — thanks for the clear options and the quick turnaround. ClearWave's position after internal discussion: they are willing to accept Option A (2x rolling annual fees) subject to one change: a narrower carve-out for security incidents that allows recovery for regulatory fines only to the extent reimbursed by Redwood's cyber insurance or proven to directly result from Redwood's gross negligence.

They also asked for a brief clause clarifying that consequential damages remain excluded except where California or other applicable law requires otherwise (they acknowledge some jurisdictions may have mandatory rules).

If Redwood can accept the insurance-linked data-breach modifier and the jurisdiction caveat on consequential damages, ClearWave will sign the Order Form and proceed to DocuSign. Please prepare the final clean copy and loop in our execution team.

Regards,
Michael Hart
Bryants & Co. LLP
